goal: The worktree retention sweep recurs on a bounded cadence while the daemon runs, so a parked worktree that ages past the retention window is reclaimed mid-run without requiring a restart while a within-window worktree survives.

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- retention_sweep() at lines 1019-1054 removes worktrees older than retention_days and their branches; the main loop calls it ONCE at boot (line 2072). Make the sweep recur on a bounded cadence inside the `while not shutdown[...]` loop (per-cycle or on an interval), preserving exactly what one sweep does.
packages/flywheel-worktree/tests/test_sandbox_retention.py -- existing retention behavior to keep green; the per-sweep removal semantics must not change, only the cadence.
constraints: Preserve retention_sweep's existing semantics exactly: prune dangling entries first, remove worktrees older than the window AND their flywheel/<phase>/<task-id> branches, leave within-window worktrees untouched. This task changes the CADENCE, not what one sweep removes.
The sweep must run on a bounded recurring cadence while the loop runs (more than the single boot invocation across N cycles / an elapsed interval) -- a boot-only sweep is the leak this task removes.
The recurring tick must be drivable in a test without a real restart (so the test asserts mid-run reclaim, not reclaim-on-restart).
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not change retention_sweep's removal rules or what counts as 'older than the window'.
Do not modify or weaken existing retention/worker tests; do not weaken assertions.
Do not touch flywheel_core purity boundaries.
edge_cases: A within-window worktree must survive every tick (the cadence must not over-reclaim).
Calling the sweep exactly once at boot must FAIL the cadence grader -- the cadence must recur across cycles.
Clock advance between ticks: a worktree that ages past the window mid-run is gone after the next tick, not only after restart.
